questions.question: Q: What is the choreographic intention of 'Emancipation of Expressionism'?
questions.correctAnswer: To demonstrate the power of expression through hip-hop dance, showing how movement can communicate freedom and serve as a form of artistic liberation.

questions.question: Q: Name three hip-hop styles featured in the work.
questions.correctAnswer: Popping, locking and krumping — though breaking and house are also featured in the movement vocabulary.

questions.question: Q: How does the structure of the work support its intention?
questions.correctAnswer: The structure builds from a single dancer to the full ensemble, symbolising how expression spreads from the individual to the collective — one voice becoming many.

questions.question: Q: What is the role of the aural setting in the work?
questions.correctAnswer: Michael Asante's score mixes beats, music and the spoken word 'emancipation', creating a powerful, driving atmosphere that energises the dancers and reinforces the theme of liberation.

questions.question: Q: Why is the costume significant in 'Emancipation of Expressionism'?
questions.correctAnswer: Urban streetwear — hoodies, tracksuits and trainers — reflects hip-hop culture and the dancers' authentic identity, grounding the work in its cultural roots.
